subject: Whistic onboarding: staggered evidence upload & ownership plan
messages:
From: Tom Lang <tom.lang@evergreenhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@evergreenhealth.com>, security@evergreenhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Whistic access + initial SIG workbook

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the quick intro call this morning. We pulled together the initial SIG workbook and would like to get our Whistic company profile live this week if possible. Our priorities are: 1) get a baseline SIG uploaded, 2) confirm who owns each evidence item on our end vs what you can provide, and 3) stagger uploads so we don't overwhelm either team.

Attached is Evergreen_SIG_Initial.xlsx (control mapping + a few sample artifacts). Can Redwood handle any of the following items as hosted proofs: SOC 2 summary page, encryption key rotation policy (redacted), and public penetration test summary? If so, call those out and we can omit duplicates from our upload.

Proposed window: incremental uploads over 3 business days starting Thursday (Nov 12). Do you have a preferred slot for a short runbook review?

Tom
Tom Lang
Head of Security Operations
Evergreen Health
attachments: Evergreen_SIG_Initial.xlsx (xlsx, 420KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Lang <tom.lang@evergreenhealth.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@evergreenhealth.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Whistic access + initial SIG workbook

Hi Tom — really appreciate the fast turnaround and the workbook. I reviewed the spreadsheet and sketched a lightweight, staggered approach that keeps short-lived uploads first and more sensitive proofs (e.g., rotation logs) for a second pass. See the plan below — I attached a short PDF with the step-by-step checklist and an ownership matrix template (karthik_whistic_instructions.pdf).

Suggested split (3 sprints):
- Sprint A (Day 1): static artifacts we can publish immediately — org chart, certificates (ISO/SOC cover pages), encryption high-level summary, public pentest summary.
- Sprint B (Day 2): control evidence that requires minimal redaction — process docs, access review spreadsheets (redacted PII).
- Sprint C (Day 3): rotation logs and scoped audit extracts (we recommend hashed indices rather than raw logs; if you prefer full logs we need a secure transfer).

Redwood-provided hosted proofs: we can provide the SOC 2 cover page PDF and a sanitized KMS rotation summary (hashed timestamps). We cannot publish customer data or raw audit logs. If you want Redwood to host the SOC summary, confirm and I will mark those rows in the attached matrix.

Runbook review: 30 minutes tomorrow (Wed Nov 10) at 10:00am PT works for our ops; are you available? If not, propose another slot.

Next steps for Evergreen:
- Fill column "Evergreen upload?" in attached XLS for Sprint A items by EOD Wednesday.
- Confirm S3 transfer vs Whistic UI upload for Sprint C artifacts. If S3, provide a prepped bucket and a short-lived service account key.

I'll coordinate our side (Neha will be point for Sprint A/B intake; Ben will handle Sprint C secure transfer).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: karthik_whistic_instructions.pdf (pdf, 130KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Lang <tom.lang@evergreenhealth.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@evergreenhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Evergreen Whistic sprint assignments

Team — looping you in with the Evergreen plan. Quick breakdown:

- Neha: own Sprint A intake (org certs, SOC cover page, public pentest PDF). Coordinate with Tom to confirm which PDFs they will upload vs we host.
- Ben: lead Sprint C secure transfer; set up one-time S3 ingest and rotate keys after transfer. Ben, reach out to infra for a short-lived PutObject policy.
- Laura: review the ownership matrix and help fill any missing control mappings (SIG->CAIQ crosswalk) — Evergreen left a handful unmapped in their workbook.

Action items (by EOD Wednesday):
- Neha: confirm list of Sprint A artifacts from the spreadsheet (comment in the shared sheet).
- Ben: provide recommended S3 bucket policy and expected key TTL (I suggested 12 hours).
- Laura: send an initial mapping doc with questions to Tom.

If anything blocks, escalate to me and I'll join sync with Evergreen. Short heads-up: they asked for a 3-day window starting Nov 12; we should be able to accommodate with this triage.

Karthik

Date: 2026-11-10T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Whistic access + initial SIG workbook

Karthik — this is great, and the staggered approach makes sense. We uploaded Sprint A artifacts into Whistic just now (org chart, SOC cover PDF, public pentest summary). Please confirm when those appear on your side.

Two clarifications:
1) For the SOC 2 cover page: yes please host that on Redwood side — we've withheld the full report for now.
2) For Sprint C secure transfer: we'll provision an S3 bucket and generate a short-lived role for Redwood access. Expect the bucket name and role ARN by EOD Monday.

We also filled column "Evergreen upload?" for Sprint A in the workbook and added notes where artifacts need redaction (column: redaction_notes). If you could update the ownership matrix and return a marked copy, that'll help close the loop.

Appreciate the team's responsiveness — Tom

--
Tom Lang
Head of Security Operations, Evergreen Health
Phone: (415) 555-0192
